title: Let Go
coreMove: Stillness grows when you do the next honest act, name what is outside your control, and stop making peace wait for praise, timing, or reply.

exampleSpecs.audience: team leads who keep checking for praise
exampleSpecs.stakes: A finished project can turn into inbox craving when the team treats a reply as proof of worth.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use an informal message exchange to show effort remaining while the grip on the outcome loosens.

exampleSpecs.audience: operators who confuse care with constant tracking
exampleSpecs.stakes: A red number can pull a person from clean action into compulsive control.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A forecast scene separates action from externals before the tracker can take over.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who meet craving in small delays
exampleSpecs.stakes: A tiny delay can show how the mind adds suffering to ordinary waiting.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Let one close observed moment teach craving and release without forcing a decision.

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders reviewing a failure after public reaction
exampleSpecs.stakes: A failed launch leaves traces of the grip that made the work worse.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A peer helps a launch lead separate repair work from status repayment.

exampleSpecs.audience: fundraisers who want a response to prove the work mattered
exampleSpecs.stakes: A live ask can turn care for the cause into hunger for reassurance.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A donor call turns when the speaker lets another person pull the ask back to the real need.

exampleSpecs.audience: executives preparing a recommendation under scrutiny
exampleSpecs.stakes: A memo can carry clean effort while refusing to manage praise in advance.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A board packet forces a choice between clean analysis and chasing approval.
